title: How Much Fiber in Hummus? 1.7g per 2 Tbsp
description: Hummus: about 1.7 g of fiber per 2 tbsp (6% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in hummus?
intro: Hummus ranks #10 of 10 beans and legumes on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in hummus by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in hummus?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists hummus, commercial at 5.5 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (2 tbsp; 30 g) therefore has about 1.7 g of fiber and 71 calories. That is 6% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 7% of a 25 g day and 4% of a 38 g day.

Hummus is a chickpea dip with tahini, lemon, and oil. It is a useful fiber add because you usually eat it with other high-fiber foods, like raw vegetables or whole wheat pita, but a standard 2-tablespoon serving on its own is modest.

sections.heading: Why a spoonful of hummus is not a serving of beans
paragraphs: A 2-tablespoon serving weighs about 30 g, and only part of that is chickpeas. Compare that with a half cup of cooked [chickpeas](/fiber-in-chickpeas) at 82 g. Most people eat more than 2 tablespoons in practice, so it helps to measure once and see what your usual scoop looks like.
Store-bought and homemade hummus vary with the ratio of chickpeas to tahini and oil. The commercial and homemade rows in the table come from two different USDA entries.

sections.heading: How hummus compares with other beans and legumes
paragraphs: Of the 10 beans and legumes on this site, hummus ranks #10 for fiber per typical serving and #10 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 2.3 g of fiber per 100 calories, in the middle of the range for the foods on this site.

Close neighbors by serving: [edamame](/fiber-in-edamame) at 8.1 g (1 cup, shelled, cooked); [green peas](/fiber-in-green-peas) at 8.8 g (1 cup, cooked); [kidney beans](/fiber-in-kidney-beans) at 11.3 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), hummus is #43 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding hummus to your day
paragraphs: The bigger win is what you dip. Carrots, bell peppers, and whole wheat pita all add their own fiber. A quarter cup of hummus with a cup of raw carrots makes a solid afternoon snack.

Example: 1/4 cup hummus, 1 cup carrots, 1 whole wheat pita. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 10.9 g of fiber, with 3.4 g from the hummus. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of hummus?
faqs.a: 5.5 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Hummus, commercial). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in hummus (1/4 cup)?
faqs.a: About 3.4 g, for 62 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.
Moderately. Two tablespoons give a gram or two, and a quarter cup gives a bit over 3 g. The fiber climbs quickly when you pair it with vegetables or whole-grain bread.

faqs.q: Does flavored hummus have different fiber?
faqs.a: Usually only slightly. Added roasted pepper, garlic, or herbs barely change the fiber. Check the label if you eat a lot of one brand.
